items.title: How to choose a note-taking app | Zettelkasten | Notion vs Roam vs Obsidian
items.description:
=====
My name is Artem, I'm a neuroscience PhD student at Harvard University. 
🌎 Website and Social links: https://kirsanov.ai/
📥 "Receptive Field" neuro-newsletter: https://artemkirsanov.substack.com/
✨ Support me on Patreon to get access to Discord community: https://patreon.com/artemkirsanov
=====

In this video I discuss most popular applications for Zettelkasten note-taking, what I recommend to get started and how to approach any new application that might come out in the future 

🕒 OUTLINE
items.why_watch: A Harvard neuroscience PhD student walks through Notion, Roam, and Obsidian specifically through the lens of Zettelkasten — the linked-note method borrowed from prolific scholar Niklas Luhmann. At under 11 minutes, it skips the app-review fluff and focuses on which tool's architecture actually matches how networked thinking works. Useful if you've tried these apps and still felt like something wasn't clicking.

news.title: How to make the perfect zaru soba, or cold soba noodles – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect
news.snippet: Hot days call for cool dinners, and these are Japan’s nutty, salty and sweet solution. Fiery or pickled accompaniments optional Although every culture craves something different in hot weather – chilled beetroot soup in Lithuania, cooling buttermilk drinks in India, gazpacho in Spain – what many of these dishes have in common is a certain soothing silkiness as they slide down the throat, plus a decent helping of salt. Japan’s zaru soba , which Namiko Hirasawa Chen of Just One Cookbook describes as her family’s “go-to meal when the summer heat and humidity soar”, is no exception.
news.blurb: Felicity Cloake unravels the art of zaru soba — those cool, nutty buckwheat noodles that make a sweltering day feel suddenly, elegantly manageable.
